Findings written to `findings.md`. Six defects introduced by the diff:

- `src/sync.py:14` — pagination off-by-one: `total_count // PAGE_SIZE` drops the last partial page (and all rows when the count is under one page).
- `src/sync.py:24` — mutable default `seen=[]` persists across calls, so future syncs skip previously processed users.
- `src/sync.py:31` — IDs are marked as seen before the UPDATE succeeds, so failed users are never retried.
- `src/sync.py:35` — f-string SQL interpolation of `email`/`id`: SQL injection plus breakage on quotes.
- `src/report.py:7` — early return on empty `users` leaks the open file handle.
- `src/report.py:11` — `email.lower().split("@")[1]` crashes on `None` emails (explicitly nullable per `db.py`) and on addresses lacking `@`; the old code handled `None` with a fallback.

I deliberately did not flag the `except Exception: pass` log removal or the missing `ORDER BY` in pagination, as those are behavior/style concerns rather than clear-cut defects on their own.
